own_solution.law: The power delivered by the rope is P = F·v = Fv cos(theta). Thus P = 40 × 3 × cos(30°) = 103.923 W. An additional upward tilt q gives P = 120 cos(30° + q) W.
assumptions: The sled moves horizontally, and the tension acts along the rope.
The stated tension and speed continue to apply after an added tilt.
Each added sentence is considered independently.

TF8CB.regime: F < q: the 40 N tension is below the rope's stated capacity.

T8FA9.regime: F < q: the 40 N tension is below the stated breaking threshold.

notes: All certified numerical answers agree with the stated relations. Additional rope tilts of 12°, 17° and 24° give 89.1774 W, 81.8398 W and 70.5342 W, respectively. All listed breaking strengths exceed 40 N. For each duration, W = F cos(theta) v t and W/t = Fv cos(theta), so time cancels. The earlier trial and the noncontacting crane introduce no stated dependency of the current rope power.
